original_value: We consider the task of fine-grained sentiment analysis from the perspective of multiple instance learning (MIL). Our neural model is trained on document sentiment labels, and learns to predict the sentiment of text segments, i.e. sentences or elementary discourse units (EDUs), without segment-level supervision. We introduce an attention-based polarity scoring method for identifying positive and negative text snippets and a new dataset which we call SpoT (as shorthand for Segment-level POlariTy annotations) for evaluating MIL-style sentiment models like ours. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance against multiple baselines, whereas a judgement elicitation study shows that EDU-level opinion extraction produces more informative summaries than sentence-based alternatives.

result.paraphrase: We address fine-grained sentiment analysis through the lens of multiple instance learning (MIL). Trained only with document-level sentiment labels, our neural model learns to predict the sentiment of text segments such as sentences or elementary discourse units (EDUs) without segment-level supervision. We propose an attention-based polarity scoring method to identify positive and negative text snippets, along with a new dataset called SpoT, short for Segment-level POlariTy annotations, to evaluate MIL-style sentiment models like ours. Experiments show it outperforms multiple baselines, and a judgement elicitation study finds that EDU-level opinion extraction yields more informative summaries than sentence-based alternatives.
